fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is not ready: quotient-state decoding alone does not certify the complete coefficient-to-port transfer operator. In BW16, using more than 16 rational lattice columns creates integer coefficient kernels unless additional independent charged rows are specified, contradicting the unsupported G7 audit.

Proposal 2's terminal-cut mechanism cannot separate NAND. Minimum weighted cut energy, even after minimizing auxiliary vertices, is submodular; for legal NAND states 011 and 101, submodularity and equal legal cost imply the false state 111 costs at most the legal cost because their intersection 001 is legal.

Proposal 3's empty-Delaunay-sphere condition certifies nearest points to one center, not closure of every port fiber or depth-two min-plus growth. Its rational Gram domain is not bounded, and alternating LP/SVP separation has no stated termination or exact Farkas guarantee.

Proposal 4 only enumerates affine matroids of rank at most four and therefore cannot establish its dimension-independent no-go claim. A result there would be a restricted theorem, not a discriminator for arbitrary FRONTIER tiles.

Proposal 6 is defeated at its stated mechanism: winding is an affine additive invariant of boundary phases, while the four NAND triples affinely span the three-bit space. An affine winding condition vanishing on every legal NAND triple also vanishes on every triple; signed cochains additionally permit cancellation rather than multiplicative growth.

Proposal 5 is the sole conditional survivor, but its current parameter family is not finite: a denominator bound does not bound numerators, and “one rational skew coupling” specifies neither matrix support nor magnitude. An antisymmetric coupling contributes nothing to a quadratic form, so the mutation must use a frozen symmetric off-block family.
evidence: No verifier evidence supports any of the six proposals; all claimed moves are prospective. Existing evidence establishes no hardness lemma or dimension-dependent gap.

ROADMAP requires equal-radius NAND/COPY completeness, complete unrestricted transfer closure on K, an exact outside-codebook certificate, and depth-two lambda/mu at least 65/64 for every integral coefficient vector.

G28 shows that favorable local costs do not suffice when exact depth-two growth fails, while G32 and G37 exhibit compatible parity states with exactly additive cost. Any accepted D4 candidate must include these states rather than merely named attacks.

D4 triality with a nonorthogonal symmetric coupling is not ruled out by G33/G34, which concern a frozen exterior-tag family, nor by the retired tensor and group-ring counterexamples. Its finite geometry permits an exact bounded falsification once the coupling family is frozen.
